# Integer-fiber affine contact certificates for maximum-mass extraction

This note gives an exact finite contact alternative at a maximum-mass
extracted source of FULL continuous dimension q=d. It proves the desired
objective-one tensor identities under two explicit additional conditions.
In general it retains a pure abnormal alternative. It also proves that a
strict affine fit is not automatic, even at a genuine global extraction
maximum. No retained-mass fraction or cap budget is inferred.

The extraction attainment and exact one-sided thickening used here are
proved in `candidate 149b5f35c717786d`,
Sections 1--2; its independent audit is
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.

## 1. The correct feasible class uses actual integer fibers only

Let C be a compact ambient convex body in R^n x R^d, d>=1. Let D subset C
be a maximum-mass feasible extraction: its mixed measure has positive
d-dimensional mass m, its true centroid is (j,c) with j integer, and its
local normalized closed-halfspace depth is at least a prescribed beta.
Write

    P={z in Z^n: |D_z|>0},    A_z=D_z,    K_z=C_z.

Every A_z and K_z in this finite index set is a full-dimensional compact
convex subset of R^d. P is lattice-convex:

    conv(P) intersect Z^n=P.                          (1)

Indeed an integer convex combination of positive d-fibers contains their
positive-volume Minkowski combination. The canonical positive-fiber hull
E=conv{(z,x):z in P,x in A_z} has exactly fibers A_z at z in P and no
other integer fibers of positive mass.

Consider the finite-fiber fitting condition

    T A_z+Bz+b subset K_z    for every z in P,         (2)

where det T>0, B is d-by-n, and b is in R^d. This is sufficient for a new
feasible extraction, even if the affine image of the ORIGINAL ambient
body D is not contained in C between integer indices.

To see this, apply (z,x)->(z,Tx+Bz+b) to E. Its hull lies in C because
all generating fibers do. At every integer base its fiber is the claimed
affine image: compatibility follows from the original compatibility and
the fact that Bz+b is affine in z. If the base hull has full rank, this
is already an ambient body. Otherwise exact one-sided thickening inside
C makes it an ambient body with precisely the same integer traces.
Consequently the new mixed source is the affine pushforward of the old
one, multiplied in mass by det T. Its true centroid is

    (j,Tc+Bj+b),

and its local normalized depth is unchanged because the affine map
preserves Lambda and sends closed halfspaces bijectively to closed
halfspaces. Global extracted maximality therefore implies

    det T<=1 whenever (2) holds and det T>0.          (3)

In particular identity T=I, B=0, b=0 is a local determinant maximum of
the finite-fiber fitting problem. This implication is valid even when
P has deficient affine rank.

## 2. Exact finite normal-or-abnormal contact equations

Use variations T=I+A, B, b. Put p=d^2+dn+d. A contact triple consists of

    z in P,  x in A_z,  u in S^(d-1),
    u dot x=h_(K_z)(u).                              (4)

All these triples form a compact set. Each is a genuine contact between
the retained and original fiber in continuous direction u. They need
not be contacts of the original AMBIENT C with a normal having a
nonzero continuous part; that stronger statement is neither used nor
asserted.

There are finitely many contact triples (z_i,x_i,u_i), nonnegative
weights lambda_i, and alpha>=0, with alpha+sum lambda_i>0, satisfying

    sum_i lambda_i u_i x_i^T=alpha I_d,
    sum_i lambda_i u_i z_i^T=0,
    sum_i lambda_i u_i=0.                            (5)

At most p+1 contact terms suffice. If alpha>0, rescale to alpha=1 and
at most p contact terms suffice. The matrix pairing is Frobenius: the
first contact gradient paired with A is u_i dot A x_i.

Here is a direct finite-dimensional proof which does not invoke a
constraint qualification. For every z,x,u, condition (2) is equivalent
to the LINEAR parameter inequality

    u dot(Ax+Bz+b)<=Delta(z,x,u),
    Delta=h_(K_z)(u)-u dot x>=0.                    (6)

Let G(z,x,u)=(u x^T,u z^T,u) and g=(I_d,0,0). If a parameter direction
v had g dot v>0 and G dot v<0 at EVERY contact, it would give a genuine
feasible small positive step. In fact compactness makes G dot v uniformly
negative on contacts and on a neighborhood of them. On the remaining
compact constraint set Delta has a positive minimum, so a sufficiently
small step satisfies those constraints too. Its determinant has positive
first derivative g dot v, contradicting (3).

It follows by elementary strict separation that zero belongs to
conv({G:contact} union {-g}). Otherwise a separating v, with its sign
chosen appropriately, would have exactly the two forbidden strict
inequalities. Thus a convex combination gives

    sum lambda_i G_i=alpha g.

Caratheodory gives finitely many terms and the stated p+1 bound (and
conic Caratheodory gives p when alpha>0). This proves (5). Since g is
nonzero, the contact weights cannot all vanish.

The same proof can be carried out in the affine span of P, of dimension
k, using centered base coordinates. Its sharper parameter dimension is
p=d^2+dk+d. The equations in the original coordinates still follow from
the centered base equation and sum lambda_i u_i=0.

## 3. Two justified ways to obtain alpha=1

### A strict fiber fit

Suppose there exist T_0,B_0,b_0 such that

    T_0 A_z+B_0z+b_0 subset int(K_z) for all z in P. (7)

No determinant condition on T_0 is needed for this qualification; a
sufficiently short segment from identity still has positive determinant.
At every contact, the direction (T_0-I,B_0,b_0) has strictly negative G
pairing. An abnormal equation sum lambda_i G_i=0 would give a strictly
negative pairing on its left and zero on its right, which is impossible.
Thus the stress from Section 2 has alpha>0 and can be normalized to one.

A sufficient condition for (7) is an affine graph q(z)=B_0z+b_0 lying
in int(K_z) for every z in P: take T_0=epsilon I for sufficiently small
positive epsilon, adjusting the displayed graph notation if necessary.
Such an affine graph is NOT automatic for convex mixed bodies.

### Finite polyhedral source and target fibers

Suppose every A_z and K_z, z in P, is a polytope. Then (2) is a finite
linear system: use every vertex x of A_z and every facet normal u of K_z.
For ANY feasible parameter (T,B,b), the segment from identity is feasible.
If trace(T-I)>0, the determinant increases on a sufficiently short initial
segment, contradicting (3). Hence identity maximizes the LINEAR objective
trace(T-I) over this polyhedron. Its finite linear-programming contact
dual gives (5) with alpha=1, even if no strict fiber fit exists.
Only initially tight vertex/facet pairs are used. Normalize each nonzero
facet normal to unit length and absorb its scale into lambda. Again at
most d^2+dk+d contacts are required.

The attainment theorem does not assert that its maximizing fibers are
polytopes. Accordingly this second result is a conditional exact normal
certificate, not a reason to discard the abnormal case in general.

## 4. What integer coupling really cancels

Under the normalized equations, for every affine continuous-valued
function q(z)=Qz+c_0 one has

    sum_i lambda_i u_i (x_i-q(z_i))^T=I_d,
    sum_i lambda_i u_i dot(x_i-q(z_i))=d.            (8)

For the unnormalized alternative, replace I_d,d by alpha I_d,alpha d.
This is an exact cancellation of arbitrary continuous translations and
integer-to-continuous affine shears, including all base first moments.
In particular the supporting-fiber identity is

    sum_i lambda_i h_(K_zi)(u_i)=alpha d.            (9)

These contact weights are not cap masses or section masses. Nor does (5)
impose cancellation of arbitrary integer coefficients a_i attached to
separately chosen ambient supporting hyperplanes. In particular no
statement such as sum lambda_i a_i dot z_i=0 follows. The concrete new
information is the full matrix identity (8), with actual INTEGER source
indices; a volume lower bound still requires additional geometry.

## 5. Exact global extraction maximum with no strict affine fit

Let n=3,d=1, fix L>1, and let C be the convex hull of the sixteen points

    (z,L z_1 z_2 z_3+epsilon),
    z in {-1,1}^3, epsilon in {-1,1}.                (10)

C is an ambient convex body. Each corner fiber is exactly
[L s_z-1,L s_z+1], where s_z=z_1z_2z_3, because a corner of the base cube
has no nontrivial convex representation by other corners. Moreover C is
centrally symmetric: (z,x)->(-z,-x) preserves the vertices. Its mixed
measure is therefore centrally symmetric, has true centroid (0,0), and
has local depth at least 1/2. Taking D=C gives a genuine GLOBAL maximum
extraction at beta=gamma_1=1/2, with all original mass retained.

If a strict fit (7) existed, its corner interval constraints would give

    |(T-1)L s_z+Bz+b|+|T|<1                       (11)

for all eight corners. Multiply the center errors by s_z and average.
The cube identities average(s_z)=average(s_z z_l)=0 imply

    |T-1| L < 1-|T|.                              (12)

If |T|>=1 the right side is nonpositive. If |T|<1, the triangle inequality
|T-1|>=1-|T|, together with L>1, contradicts (12). Hence no strict affine
fit exists, even allowing arbitrary real T.

This does not refute the normal certificate: the two contacts of any
one corner interval, each with weight 1/2 and normals +1,-1, already give
sum lambda u x=1 and the other two balances zero. It proves specifically
that an automatic Slater argument is unavailable even at a true optimum.

## 6. Why one must discard artificial between-fiber constraints

For comparison, let n=d=1 and

    C={(z,x):0<=z<=2, |x|<=sqrt(z)},
    D={(z,x):0<=z<=3/2, |x|<=sqrt(z)-z/2}.           (13)

These are compact ambient convex bodies and D subset C. Any AMBIENT fit
(z,x)->(z,Tx+Bz+b) must have b=0 at z=0. Its width constraint gives

    |T|(sqrt(z)-z/2)<=sqrt(z) for z>0,

so |T|<=1 by z decreasing to zero. Identity is feasible, hence it is an
affine determinant maximum in this restricted ambient-fit family.
However D touches the boundary of C only at (0,0). Every supporting
normal of C there has continuous component u=0: C has local description
z>=x^2, and the unique normal ray at the vertex is (-1,0). Thus every
ambient contact gradient is zero and a normalized finite certificate
is impossible.

D is NOT a global extracted-mass maximum. Its only positive integer
fiber is the interval [-1/2,1/2] at z=1, and that fiber can be doubled
inside C. The source-only model of Section 1 detects this improvement
and has no such false maximum. This diagnostic refutes exact normality
from ambient affine maximality alone; it does not settle whether the
abnormal alternative in Section 2 can occur without a normal certificate
at a genuine globally maximum extracted source.

The unconditional proved result is the finite integer-fiber alternative
(5), plus normality under (7) or finite polyhedral source/target data.
General objective-one normality and any sharp retained-mass inequality
remain unproved.
